exposure: behavioral characteristics (e.g., tobacco and alcohol use)
pregnancy characteristics (e.g., season and year of delivery)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1028 live singleton births delivered between 2011 and 2017 to pregnant women recruited from the heavily contaminated Northern coast of Puerto Rico who were free of pre-existing conditions like diabetes.
finding: Socioeconomic status and high pre-pregnancy BMI were associated with higher preterm birth rates, while tobacco use during pregnancy increased the odds of small for gestational age delivery among pregnant women in Puerto Rico.
